title: A sweep node draws an arrow that leaves and arrives in set directions
body:
Today `arrow { route curve; }` draws a cubic whose handles leave each end along its side, or along the longer axis at a bare point. `Connector::handles` in `crates/acre/src/scene/connector.rs` gives a side's handle a reach of half the arrow's full length. An arrow much wider than it is tall then gets handles far longer than its height. Between a `bottom` and a `top`, the curve dips below its target and climbs back up into it. A file cannot give a bare point a direction, so a figure names an invisible box at each end to get vertical ends.

## Proposal

A new node kind, `sweep`, draws one cubic from `from` to `to`.

- `from` and `to` take a point or `NAME SIDE`, as on `arrow`.
- `leave DIR` and `enter DIR`, with DIR one of `up`, `down`, `left` and `right`, give the direction of travel at a bare end. An end that names a side takes the side's direction. An end with neither, or with both, is an error.
- Each handle reaches half the distance between the ends, measured along its own direction. Between `leave down` and `enter down` the curve only moves down. When the other end lies behind a direction or level with it, that handle reaches half the full length, as on `arrow`.
- `stroke`, `stroke-width`, `dash`, `head`, `tail` and `head-size` work as on `arrow`, and the head is a triangle by default. `sweep` takes no `route`, `repeat` or label.

`sweep` builds a `Connector` with a route of its own, so it shares drawing, heads and following moved things with `arrow`.

## Rejected

- Changing the reach for `route curve`. Every figure with a curve between sides would redraw.
